findings.summary: Fixed-evidence, 63-session research comparison: NVDA has the stronger reported data-center acceleration and better completed 63-session behavior versus QQQ; MU has exceptional reported interim earnings but materially higher volatility and weaker completed 63-session relative behavior. Both company valuations are explicitly conditional scenario sensitivities, not consensus or fair-value estimates. QQQ provides diversification but retains dated look-through weights in both names and an aggregate fund P/E that is not directly comparable with company EPS grids.

claims.text: NVDA reported Q2 FY2027 revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% year over year, Data Center revenue of $89.0 billion, up 117%, and GAAP diluted EPS of $2.46. Reported first-half FY2027 diluted EPS was $4.85, versus FY2026 annual diluted EPS of $4.90; the interim result is not annualized.

NVDA FY2027 US-GAAP split-adjusted sensitivity assumes EPS/multiples of $7.50/25x, $9.00/30x, and $10.50/35x. The resulting bear/base/bull prices and percentage changes from the September 18 split-adjusted close are in the NVDA scenario grid; inputs are assumptions, not consensus, observed P/E, or forecasts.

NVDA's completed 63-session price return was 5.50% versus QQQ's -2.59%, a calculated +8.08 percentage-point excess return; its 63-session realized volatility was 39.63% versus QQQ's 20.85%. These are descriptive, not predictive.

MU reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $41.46 billion, GAAP net income of $28.24 billion, and GAAP diluted EPS of $24.67. Its reported 273-day FY2026 interim diluted EPS was $41.40 versus FY2025 annual diluted EPS of $7.59; the interim figure is not annualized.

MU FY2026 US-GAAP split-adjusted sensitivity assumes EPS/multiples of $35/18x, $45/22x, and $55/26x. The resulting bear/base/bull prices and percentage changes from the September 18 split-adjusted close are in the MU scenario grid; inputs are assumptions, not consensus, observed P/E, or forecasts.
MU's completed 63-session price return was -10.42% versus QQQ's -2.59%, a calculated -7.83 percentage-point excess return; its 63-session realized volatility was 89.56% versus QQQ's 20.85%.

QQQ's dated September 18 equity holdings assigned 8.54% to NVDA and 5.01% to MU, with 99.86% reported equity-weight coverage. Sponsor-reported aggregate P/E was 30.08x as of August 31. These are dated fund metrics and are not comparable to company EPS-grid assumptions.

NVDA disclosed export-control harm, effective foreclosure from the China market, and dependence on overseas partners, especially Taiwan and South Korea. MU disclosed potential tariff/trade-restriction risk. The supplied January rule moved specified advanced-semiconductor review to case-by-case subject to conditions, without quantifying issuer impact or establishing later policy status.

gaps.description: No verified policy status subsequent to the January 2026 rule or quantified issuer-specific revenue, earnings, or supply-chain impact. This blocks a quantified policy-impact conclusion but not disclosed operating facts or conditional scenario math.
No forward consensus or observed issuer P/E is supplied. Company valuation conclusions are therefore conditional on the stated scenario EPS and multiple assumptions rather than fair-value estimates.

assumptions: Company grids use US-GAAP annual EPS and declared split-adjusted share-basis assumptions; annual reported EPS and interim EPS are anchors, not annualizations.
NVDA base sensitivity requires continued data-center demand conversion and margin resilience; MU base sensitivity requires retention of much of the reported interim earnings strength after fiscal Q3.
QQQ comparison uses dated sponsor holdings and an aggregate sponsor P/E, not synthetic corporate EPS, current holdings, or inferred fund exposures.
findings.counter_thesis: NVDA's acceleration may not persist amid customer concentration, export controls, and overseas-supply dependence. MU's record earnings may moderate sharply with memory-cycle, customer, tariff, and execution risks. QQQ's diversification can be preferable if either single-name case fails, though its dated holdings retain exposure to both companies.

review_conditions.description: Review NVDA's next results for Data Center revenue, GAAP EPS, customer concentration, and material export-control or supply disclosures; material deterioration would challenge the base sensitivity.
Review MU's September 30 fiscal-Q4 results for earnings, strategic-customer agreements, cash generation, and capex relative to the FY2026 sensitivity assumptions.
Refresh QQQ sponsor holdings and aggregate valuation before relying on fund look-through comparisons because composition and characteristics are dated.

instruments.thesis: Reported Data Center acceleration and positive completed 63-session excess return versus QQQ support a conditional case, subject to continuation of demand and margins.
instruments.counter_thesis: Export controls, customer concentration, overseas supply dependence, or demand moderation could invalidate the earnings/multiple assumptions.
